summary.description: Project 6: Zero-Knowledge Password Manager — Week 1 threat model

diagrams.title: Project 6: Zero-Knowledge Password Manager — Week 1 threat model diagram

threats.title: T-20 Weak Master Password
threats.description: The user chooses a weak master password, allowing an attacker to brute-force the Argon2id derivation and gain access to the entire vault.
threats.mitigation: Enforce a strict password strength meter during registration and use high-memory Argon2id parameters.

threats.title: T-21 Server Dependency Exploit
threats.description: An attacker exploits a known vulnerability in an unpatched Node.js or Express dependency to gain unauthorized control over the server process.
threats.mitigation: Run npm audit in CI, keep dependencies updated, and run the server as a non-root user in Docker.

threats.title: T-14 Phishing Through Browser Frame Impersonation
threats.description: An attacker creates a fraudulent webpage or embedded browser frame that imitates a trusted website, attempting to trick the password manager into automatically filling stored login credentials into an unauthorized website.
threats.mitigation: Verify the exact website origin before automatically filling passwords, including the communication scheme, hostname, and port number. Reject unauthorized embedded frames and require additional user confirmation when necessary.

threats.title: T-22 Database Storage Exhaustion
threats.description: An attacker or buggy client fills the database with massive amounts of ciphertext, exhausting disk space and causing a system outage.
threats.mitigation: Implement strict per-user storage quotas, maximum upload sizes, and database disk-space monitoring.

threats.title: T-12 Encrypted Vault Synchronization Flooding
threats.description: An attacker repeatedly uploads extremely large encrypted data files to the synchronization service, exhausting server storage, bandwidth, or processing resources.
threats.mitigation: Enforce maximum request body sizes, user storage quotas, upload limits, and request rate limiting to prevent excessive resource consumption.

threats.title: T-07 Master Password Theft
threats.description: A malicious script attempts to capture the user's master password when it is entered into the browser extension, potentially exposing access to the entire password vault.
threats.mitigation: Use isolated execution environments provided by Manifest Version 3 browser extensions and enforce a strict Content Security Policy to reduce unauthorized script execution.

data.name:
DF-9 — Structured Query Language 
Encrypted Data

threats.title: T-03 Encrypted Vault Data Modification
threats.description: An attacker deliberately changes individual bits of encrypted password vault information stored in the PostgreSQL database, potentially corrupting the stored data.
threats.mitigation: Use the Extended ChaCha20 stream cipher with Poly1305 message authentication to detect unauthorized modifications to encrypted information.

threats.title: T-08 Database and Server Log Information Theft
threats.description: An attacker gains unauthorized access to the PostgreSQL database and server logs, copying stored encrypted vault information and potentially sensitive account metadata.
threats.mitigation: Implement a zero-knowledge security architecture in which vault information is encrypted on the user's device and the server never receives the master password, plaintext vault contents, or decryption keys.

threats.title: T-15 Unauthorized Access to Another User's Vault
threats.description: An authenticated attacker manipulates password vault record identifiers to access encrypted information belonging to another user because the server fails to verify record ownership.
threats.mitigation: Use parameterized Structured Query Language statements and enforce server-side ownership verification using the authenticated user's unique identifier for every vault operation.

labels:
DF-9 — Structured Query Language 
Encrypted Data

threats.title: T-18 Encrypted Password Vault Rollback Attack
threats.description: A compromised server returns an outdated but correctly encrypted version of a user's password vault, potentially restoring old passwords or outdated security settings without the user's knowledge.
threats.mitigation: Include a version number in the Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data metadata and compare it against a trusted version record to detect attempts to restore outdated vault information.

threats.title: T-04 Emergency Recovery Timer Manipulation
threats.description: A malicious administrator changes the waiting period for emergency account recovery to allow encrypted recovery information to be released earlier than authorized.
threats.mitigation: Use cryptographically signed timestamps and a server-controlled state machine to enforce the correct emergency recovery waiting period.

threats.title: T-06 Denial of Emergency Recovery Activity
threats.description: An emergency contact performs an account recovery action but later denies having requested or completed that action.
threats.mitigation: Maintain tamper-evident audit logs and use authenticated digital signatures to provide reliable evidence of emergency recovery actions.

threats.title: T-13 Unauthorized Emergency Recovery Access
threats.description: An attacker exploits weaknesses in the emergency recovery process to bypass the required waiting period and gain access to recovery information before authorization is granted.
threats.mitigation: Enforce emergency recovery rules on the server using atomic state transitions and database transactions so that recovery requests cannot bypass required authorization checks or waiting periods.

threats.title: T-09 — Password Hash Disclosure to Have I Been Pwned
threats.description: The browser extension accidentally transmits the complete Secure Hash Algorithm 1 password hash to the Have I Been Pwned service, unnecessarily exposing information about the user's password.
threats.mitigation: Use the Have I Been Pwned range application programming interface with the k-anonymity technique. Send only the first five hexadecimal characters of the password hash and perform the remaining comparison locally on the user's device.

threats.title: T-05 Denial of Password Sharing Activity
threats.description: A user shares an encrypted password or vault item with another user but later denies performing the sharing operation.
threats.mitigation: Require users to digitally sign password-sharing transactions and maintain tamper-resistant records of sharing activities.

threats.title: T-17 Authentication Registration Replay Attack
threats.description: An attacker captures previously transmitted registration messages and attempts to send them again to the server to impersonate a legitimate registration request or interfere with account creation.
threats.mitigation: Implement server-side replay protection for the OPAQUE registration process, including authenticated registration sessions, prevention of unauthorized registration record replacement, and rejection of duplicate or invalid requests.

threats.title: T-16 Modification of Encrypted Sharing Information
threats.description: An attacker intercepts and modifies an encrypted sharing envelope while it is being delivered from the server to the intended recipient, potentially corrupting or manipulating the shared information.
threats.mitigation: Protect the encrypted sharing envelope using Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data and verify its authentication tag before accepting or decrypting the information.

threats.title: T-02 Public Key Impersonation
threats.description: An attacker replaces a legitimate user's Curve25519 public key with a fraudulent key, potentially allowing the attacker to receive encrypted information intended for another user.
threats.mitigation: Use cryptographic digital signatures to verify the authenticity and ownership of public keys before sharing encrypted information.

data.name:

One-Time Password Information

threats.title: T-10 One-Time Password Secret Leakage
threats.description: A secret key used to generate time-based one-time authentication passwords is accidentally transmitted or stored without encryption, potentially allowing an attacker to generate valid authentication codes.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt each time-based one-time password secret using its dedicated vault item encryption key before sending it to the server.

OPAQUE Authentication Protocol

threats.title: T-01 — Man-in-the-Middle Attack
threats.description: An attacker intercepts communication between the browser extension and the server and attempts to impersonate the legitimate server during the OPAQUE authentication process.
threats.mitigation: Enforce Transport Layer Security version 1.3 and use the OPAQUE password-authenticated key exchange protocol with proper server authentication.

threats.title: T-11 Authentication Service Flooding
threats.description: An attacker sends an excessive number of authentication requests to the server, consuming computing resources and preventing legitimate users from signing into their accounts.
threats.mitigation: Implement request rate limiting based on users' Internet Protocol addresses and individual accounts, together with request timeouts and resource limits.
